C53543.observed: What was checked: that the shop's choice of look governs all six kinds of customer paperwork, and that none of them keeps a look of its own. What happened: all six follow the current choice. Each was produced twice, once with the shop on the old look and once on the new, and each came out in whichever look was selected at the time, with its number and its money unchanged. The estimate and the work order invoice, on a paid job: the new-look version carries large section headings the old one does not, while shop supplies $318.13, subtotal $4,623.35, total $4,854.52 and balance $0.00 read the same in both. The parts sale invoice: invoice number INV-P2-242 and subtotal $21.85, total $22.94 identical in both. The parts sale estimate: same document number in both, and not one money figure present in one version and missing from the other. The credit invoice: CM-103, which credits invoice INV-S-3, printed 'Credit To' in ordinary type on the old look and ADDRESSES and CREDIT TO as headings on the new, with the returned parts at -$500.00 and -$125.00 unchanged. The parts sale credit: CM-2177, which credits parts sale invoice INV-P-54 for Derrick's Mobile Truck Repair, behaved the same way - old look 'Credit To' and 'Credit Number / Status / Invoice Number' in ordinary type, new look the same information under large headings - with the returned brake parts at -$419.98 and -$251.98 identical in both. Two further parts sale credits, CM-2190 and CM-2191, were produced the same way on both looks and behaved identically.
